la-04v1.title: Landscape: very flat, slightly red soil
la-04v1.summary: Very flat, with mountains only visible across the river in Thailand. The soil has a slight red tinge, less red than the south.

differs.how: Thailand has the mountains across the river, Laos is flat

la-3hIR.title: Sign: stop sign with two characters
la-3hIR.summary: Stop signs use local script, sometimes with 'stop' in Latin letters below. Here the word has 2 characters, versus 3 in Thailand.

la-HOpP.title: Landscape: big river with low hills
la-HOpP.summary: A town on a large river (the Mekong) surrounded by low mountains and hills, which are not always visible.

la-IN2F.title: Bollard: red and white concrete block
la-IN2F.summary: A red and white painted concrete block sits a few metres off the side of the road.

la-Iall.title: Poles: red-white diagonal stripes, not to base
la-Iall.summary: Some lamp posts have diagonal red and white stripes that stop above the base.

la-KUIb.title: Road: divided highway of concrete blocks
la-KUIb.summary: A road east of the capital made entirely of concrete blocks, and one of very few divided highways with coverage.

la-LUJM.title: Driving side: right
la-LUJM.summary: Traffic drives on the right. Handy against Thailand next door, which drives on the left.

la-LsED.title: Trekker: huge war memorial arch
la-LsED.summary: The only trekker coverage shows a massive war memorial arch (Patuxai) in the capital, taken on foot or with a tripod.

la-N7h9.title: Plate: short and yellow
la-N7h9.summary: Short yellow plates on normal cars. Thailand and Cambodia use white plates on private cars. Commercial plates here are white and government ones blue.

differs.how: Thai private cars have white plates
Cambodian private cars have white plates

la-QR2a.title: Landscape: red soil and dry hills
la-QR2a.summary: Distinct red soil, unusually dry plants and dry hills nearby, in the south.

la-VMbz.title: Bollard: square concrete, black and white bands
la-VMbz.summary: Square concrete bollards painted white with one or more black bands. Thailand, Indonesia and rarely Cambodia use similar ones.

la-Vgk1.title: Sign back: blue
la-Vgk1.summary: Blue sign backs only occur in this one town, the old royal capital.

la-XxPH.title: Road: striped curbs in many colours
la-XxPH.summary: Curbs painted in stripes such as red, yellow, or black with white are common.

la-fEd7.title: Landscape: hilly, dry forest road with curbs
la-fEd7.summary: A good road through a conservation area: unusually hilly, dry and forested, with coloured curbs and dashed outer lines. The only single road with black-white or yellow-white curbs.

la-fIJW.title: Plants: palm trees in the old royal town
la-fIJW.summary: Palm trees are common in this town, the former royal capital.

la-gwui.title: Google car: none visible, rural capital area
la-gwui.summary: The capital area is the only part where the Google car is not visible, and it has a lot of rural coverage. It can be a toss-up with Thailand and Cambodia, so use driving side.

differs.how: Thailand drives on the left, Laos on the right
Cambodia drives on the right too, so use other clues

la-lqdo.title: Google car: silver, two-bar roof rack
la-lqdo.summary: Silver car with a roof rack of two metal bars and black side mirrors. Seen in every city except the capital. Guatemala has a similar car, so check other clues.

la-oTVy.title: Landscape: rugged mountain range everywhere
la-oTVy.summary: A jagged mountain range is visible from almost anywhere in the town and is the best way to recognise it. Coverage here is tiny and lies south of the map label.

la-ootv.title: Signs: lots of hotels and guesthouses
la-ootv.summary: A very touristy town with many hotel and guesthouse signs. Useful in the few rounds where buildings hide the mountains.

la-p67D.title: Religion: Buddhist temples with gold leaf
la-p67D.summary: A mostly Buddhist country, with ornate temples often decorated in gold leaf. Thailand and Cambodia are Buddhist too, so it does not separate them.

la-q4i1.title: Language: compact curvy script
la-q4i1.summary: Compact, curvy letters with marks above and below. Looks like Thai but with fewer straight lines in most fonts.

differs.how: Thai script has more straight lines

la-rwz1.title: Pole: square concrete with pinholes
la-rwz1.summary: Square concrete poles with a row of small holes down the sides. Thailand and Sri Lanka use similar poles, Cambodia less often.

la-sHs4.title: Flags: red hammer and sickle
la-sHs4.summary: A communist country, so you can sometimes see red flags with a hammer and sickle.

la-uXJP.title: Houses: old temples, dark wood, French colonial
la-uXJP.summary: A UNESCO heritage town with temples, buildings using traditional dark wood, and some French colonial buildings.

la-vRr8.title: Road: divided highway with side street lamps
la-vRr8.summary: A divided highway recognisable by street lamps along its sides. The divided part of road 13 has the same lamps but is more urban with a different road angle.

la-wMAB.title: Coverage: only five cities, all Gen 3
la-wMAB.summary: Coverage is very limited: five cities, all Gen 3. Each looks different: old town with hills and palms, jagged mountains, big capital without roof rack, very flat, or red soil and dry hills.

la-ztlX.title: Coverage: 1380 m bridge over big river
la-ztlX.summary: A 1380-metre bridge over the Mekong next to the southern city. It is the only major bridge in Laos with coverage.
